comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C32-C37 regarding Shh+/− mice experiments. Both evaluations find the genetic approaches rigorous and the evidence for Shh's contribution to seizure-induced neurogenesis convincing. OpenEval notes residual neurogenesis suggesting additional factors; peer reviewers do not raise concerns about this interpretation.

Perfect alignment on claims C38-C47 regarding mossy cell identification as Shh source. Both evaluations praise the rigorous genetic approaches (ShhEGFP-Cre/+ mice) and lineage tracing combined with RNAscope. Peer reviewers specifically commend the study as 'extremely well done' with adequate consideration of statistics and artifact avoidance.

Perfect alignment on claims C69-C74 regarding contralateral effects and Shh transport. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes the lack of direct transport evidence; peer reviewers do not raise concerns and praise the overall methodological rigor including statistics and artifact avoidance.

Perfect alignment on claims C89-C95 regarding aging effects. Both evaluations support the findings. Peer reviewer notes the aging analysis is 'not well connected with the rest of the study' (presentation issue) but does not question data validity. OpenEval finds evidence strong for Shh's role in maintaining NSC pool during aging.

Perfect alignment on claims C98-C99 regarding residual neurogenesis indicating Shh is not the sole mediator. Both evaluations support this interpretation as scientifically sound and appropriate acknowledgment of data limitations.

Strong alignment on claims C28-C29, C31 regarding Gli1-LacZ reporter and seizure-induced Shh signaling activation. OpenEval also includes C30 in evaluation. Both find the genetic approaches rigorous and convincing, with peer reviewers noting 'compelling and impactful' results.

Strong alignment on claims C58-C65 regarding DREADD experiments showing activity-dependent control of neurogenesis. OpenEval R6 covers C58-C65; peer R5 covers C58-C68 (including Shh requirement claims). Both evaluations praise the DREADD approach as convincing evidence for the activity-dependent mechanism.

Partial overlap on claims C66-C68 regarding Shh requirement for activity-induced neurogenesis. OpenEval R7 specifically addresses these claims; peer R5 groups them with broader DREADD findings (C58-C68). Both evaluations support the evidence as strong and well-executed.

Alignment on claims C48-C52 regarding conditional knockout showing mossy cell-derived Shh as major source. Peer R4 also includes C53-C57 (seizure-induced neurogenesis effects). Both evaluations praise the conditional knockout approach as compelling and rigorous, treating it as a key strength.

Alignment on claims C53-C57 regarding reduced seizure-induced neurogenesis in Shh-cKO mice. OpenEval R5 focuses specifically on these claims; peer R4 groups them with C48-C52 (conditional knockout findings). Both evaluations find the evidence clear and convincing.

Strong alignment on claims C75-C81 regarding BrdU retention and NSC self-renewal. Peer R7 also includes C82-C87 (NSC pool maintenance). Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers specifically commending the 'stringent methods and analysis' including BrdU pulse-chase.

Strong alignment on claims C82-C87 regarding NSC pool maintenance. OpenEval R10 focuses on these claims; peer R7 groups them with C75-C81 (self-renewal findings). Both evaluations find the evidence robust, with peer reviewers praising the stringent BrdU pulse-chase methodology.
